metadata.title: The Rise of SK Hynix: An Absurd Chaebol Saga Choking Global AI
metadata.guest_role: SV101 host · Dihao Li (chaebol gossip segment)

conclusion: On July 10, 2026 SK hynix listed Nasdaq ADRs (SKHY), raising $26.5B — the largest foreign US IPO — with market cap past $1T. The arc runs textiles → oil/telecom monopolies → SK's 2011 Hynix rescue, the AMD HBM bet, 2022 HBM3 for H100, and MR-MUF edge over Samsung TC-NCF. 2026 HBM is sold out into 2027+ with >20% wafer gap possibly through 2030; 58% share but Samsung and Micron close in. Chaebol politics and Chey's divorce frame a Korean story — HBM is real, memory cyclicality still lurks.
background:
SK hynix ADRs opened ~19% above offer; Jensen Huang met Chey Tae-won for the fourth time in six months. The narrative covers chaebol history (Chey Jong-hyon's textile start, 1980 Korea Oil swallow, 1994 Korea Mobile), the 1999 forced Hyundai–LG chip merger birthing Hynix, Micron's failed 2002 takeover, and SK's 2011 ~$3.05B bid for 21.1%.

Tech arc: 2013 AMD HBM co-development; 2021–22 HBM3 ramp aligned with AI; 2024 HBM3E on H200/B200; 2026 HBM4 shipping to Vera Rubin.
important_facts: HBM and the memory wall: compute doubles ~every 18 months vs memory bandwidth ~every 10 years — the 1994 'Hitting the Memory Wall' paper predicted systems would stall on data moves. HBM uses 3D stack + TSV + SK's MR-MUF mass-reflow underfill for bandwidth; thermal bumps can be ~4× Samsung TC-NCF, making HBM a prerequisite for AI train/infer and agent workloads — swapping vendors requires joint re-qualification with NVDA and TSMC CoWoS.

Competition and supply: 2026 Q1 SK hynix ~58% HBM revenue share (down from ~69%), Samsung/Micron ~21% each; SK holds ~60–70% of Rubin HBM4 orders. Each HBM wafer costs ~3 conventional DRAM wafers; 2026 HBM output fully booked into 2027+; Chey cites >20% wafer gap possibly through 2030. Cheongju M15X H2 2026, Yongin from 2027, Indiana packaging H2 2028 — ~$29B ADR raise expands capacity but meaningful supply lands ~2028.

Chaebol origins and capital events: Sun Kyung textiles acquired Korea Oil (1980) and Korea Mobile (1994); 1999 state-forced Hyundai–LG chip merger birthed Hynix; SK bought 21.1% in 2011 for ~$3.05B. July 10, 2026 SKHY Nasdaq listing raised $26.5B, a foreign IPO record. Chey Tae-won vs Roh So-young divorce — a KRW 1.38T split reversed on supreme-court appeal — limited direct SK hynix impact but underscores political capital in SK's rise.

mental_model.name: Memory Wall × Second-Place Bet × Storage Cycle
mental_model.components: AI FLOPs outrun bandwidth — HBM is the shovel handle on NVDA's pickaxe; without it GPUs idle. Perennial #2 players (SK vs Samsung, AMD vs NVDA) chase edge tech and deep customer quals; MR-MUF one-shot molding beats Samsung TC-NCF layer-by-layer heat press on 12–16-stack heat and yield. Storage stays capex-heavy and cyclical — DRAM/NAND ASPs up 60–70% in places, yet memory has repeatedly re-rated down after 'this time is different' hype.
mental_model.application: Underwrite AI infra beyond GPUs: track HBM capacity, packaging yield, and second-source qualification. SKHY ADR adds liquidity and funds expansion, but supply lags ~2 years; watch Samsung NVDA sign-off, Micron CHIPS onshoring, and 2028 supply-driven pricing resets.

key_insights.question: Why can't Nvidia swap vendors easily?
key_insights.answer: HBM needs joint validation on packaging, thermals, signal integrity and TSMC CoWoS — SK hynix's HBM3 MR-MUF heat path and yield won first H100 qualification, often the sole early supplier.

key_insights.question: Why did Huang sign 'Please Make More'?
key_insights.answer: Agent infer demand plus each HBM die cannibalizes ~3 DRAM wafers; Chey cites >20% wafer gap, orders into 2027+, customers offering to prepay EUV tools.

key_insights.view: Respect the cycle beneath 'this time is different.'
key_insights.question: How to read the ADR?
key_insights.answer: Markets price SK hynix as an AI infra toll booth, but memory has repeatedly re-rated down after super-cycle hype; HBM demand is real, yet share erosion and 2028 supply could compress margins.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Primary HBM supplier with sold-out 2026 capacity and MR-MUF lead; ADR listing eases Korea discount and funds ~$29B expansion — supply tight through ~2028 but share slipped 69%→58%
GPU shipments hard-linked to HBM3/4/4E quals and deep SK co-development; Jensen's Korea visits signal memory — not just silicon — gates AI infra upside
Only US memory maker with CHIPS funding and improving HBM4 yields; smaller scale than SK/Samsung but benefits from supply-chain localization as NVDA's #2/#3 HBM source
